steps.thought: I will list all available tests on the station to understand what diagnostic tools can be used to evaluate the drone subsystems.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run the power_on_selftest to quickly check all communication buses and initial device enumeration across all subsystems.
steps.observation: The power_on_selftest passed successfully with all devices found on I2C, UART, and CAN, leaving the unit as a healthy candidate or requiring further tests across all subsystems to isolate any hidden faults.

hypotheses.rationale: Initial power on self-test passed without any errors or missing devices.
Only the system boot test has been run; comprehensive tests on all subsystems are required to confirm health or reveal a specific fault.

steps.thought: I need to check the battery health next as part of covering all subsystems to confirm the unit is healthy or find a hidden battery fault.
steps.observation: The battery_rest_check passed successfully with normal cell voltages and minimal imbalance. Further subsystem tests are needed to cover all components before confirming the unit is healthy.

hypotheses.rationale: Power on self-test and battery rest check both passed without any failures or abnormal readings.
Only system and battery subsystems have been checked; tests on esc, compass, harness, camera, imu, and motors are still required.

steps.thought: I will run the esc_telemetry test to check the ESC subsystem for sync errors and communication issues as part of covering all subsystems.
steps.observation: The ESC telemetry test passed successfully for all four ESCs with no sync errors, low packet loss, and normal temperatures, ruling out ESC commutation or thermal faults.

hypotheses.rationale: Power-on selftest, battery rest check, and ESC telemetry all passed with normal readings.
Remaining subsystems such as compass, harness, camera, IMU, and motors still need to be tested before confirming the unit is fully healthy.

steps.thought: I need to test the compass subsystem to check for any static errors or interference before concluding the unit is healthy.
steps.observation: The compass_static test passed successfully with a minor heading error of -2.12 degrees and normal field magnitude, ruling out static compass distortion.

hypotheses.rationale: Power-on selftest, battery rest check, ESC telemetry, and static compass tests have all passed successfully.
Remaining subsystems like harness, camera, IMU, motors, and dynamic compass interference still need testing.

steps.thought: I will run the harness_continuity test to check CAN bus termination and per-bus continuity resistance as part of covering all untested subsystems.
steps.observation: The harness_continuity test passed successfully, confirming proper bus continuity and a valid CAN bus termination resistance of 59.7 ohms.

hypotheses.rationale: System, battery, ESC, compass, and harness subsystems have all been tested and passed successfully.
Remaining untested subsystems include camera, IMU, motors, and dynamic compass interference.

steps.thought: I need to test the camera subsystem next to ensure it has no hidden faults before concluding the unit is healthy.
steps.observation: The camera_selftest passed successfully with a valid sensor ID, stable frame rate, and zero CSI CRC errors, confirming the camera subsystem is healthy.

hypotheses.rationale: System, battery, ESC, compass, harness, and camera subsystems have all been tested and passed successfully.
Remaining untested subsystems include IMU, motors, and dynamic compass interference.

steps.thought: I will run the imu_static test to check the IMU subsystem, since all other checked subsystems have passed and the IMU is untested.
steps.observation: The imu_static test passed successfully with zero dropped samples, low gyro bias, and normal accelerometer noise, confirming the IMU subsystem is healthy.

hypotheses.rationale: System, battery, ESC, compass, harness, camera, and IMU subsystems have all been tested and passed successfully with no failures.
Remaining untested subsystems include motors and dynamic compass interference under throttle.

steps.thought: I need to test the motor_spin_test to cover the motor subsystem, which is the last major untested subsystem, to confirm the unit is fully healthy.
steps.observation: The motor_spin_test failed because motor_1 drew 5.58 A, which is outside the acceptable range of 3.4-5.0 A, while also showing elevated temperature and RPM jitter. This indicates a potential winding short or mechanical resistance in motor_1.

hypotheses.rationale: Motor 1 shows abnormally high current draw (5.58 A), elevated temperature (53.4 C), and higher RPM jitter compared to the other motors, strongly pointing toward an electrical winding short or mechanical drag.
Elevated current draw and higher temperature on motor_1 could also stem from mechanical friction caused by a degraded bearing.

steps.thought: Since motor_1 failed the motor_spin_test due to high current and elevated temperature, let's search the failure library for similar motor current anomalies to confirm whether it is a winding short or degraded bearing.

args.query: motor_1 current high temperature elevated rpm jitter

matches.title: Motor current high on two motors, propellers unbalanced
matches.symptom_summary: Two motors show elevated current and rpm jitter at speed with propellers installed. With propellers removed the spin test passes.
matches.root_cause: Out-of-balance propellers from a bad molding batch.
matches.rework_notes: Swap propellers. The station spin test runs without propellers, so this should not appear there.

matches.title: Motor current high after propeller strike
matches.symptom_summary: One motor draws high current and runs hot after a drop at the previous station; rpm slightly low. Visible bent shaft.
matches.rework_notes: Historical variant of FL-002 caused by handling damage.

matches.title: Motor runs warm and draws extra current at normal speed
matches.symptom_summary: One motor draws roughly 30 percent more current than the others at 50 percent throttle while rpm stays within spec. Temperature a bit higher than peers but under the limit. Slight increase in rpm jitter. Gritty feel when spun by hand.
matches.root_cause: Worn or contaminated motor bearing adding mechanical drag.
matches.rework_notes: Replace the motor. Rpm in spec separates this from a winding short.

steps.observation: The motor_spin_test failed due to high current draw (5.58 A), elevated temperature (53.4 C), and increased RPM jitter on motor_1. This specifically points to a motor-level defect such as a winding short or a degraded bearing.

hypotheses.rationale: Motor 1 exhibits high current draw and elevated temperature and jitter, which are classic signs of a partial winding short.
Mechanical drag from a degraded bearing on motor_1 can also produce elevated current draw and higher temperatures.

steps.thought: Proposing rework to replace motor 1 based on the elevated current draw, high temperature, and RPM jitter observed in the motor spin test.
steps.observation: Rework applied; full suite passed: True.
